input.rationale: Mg-Sb-O is made of wide-gap phases: MgO, MgSb2O6 trirutile and Mg4Sb2O9. None of these should absorb 2.4 eV photons, so EQE was expected to be close to zero across the whole line, and the measurements confirmed this. The highest value was at the Sb-rich end, index 29 (Sb 0.807): 0.00096%, about 5x the next-highest value (index 25, 0.0002%). This fits with Sb-oxide phases such as Sb2O4 or Sb6O13, which may absorb weakly at this photon energy, becoming more common as Sb increases.

content.text:
The campaign is finished and submitted: I picked **index 29 (Sb fraction 0.807)** as the best composition, but its EQE was only 0.00096%. Nothing on this line is really photoactive at 2.4 eV.

I spent all 5 EQE measurements on a spread across the line, since I expected the Mg–Sb–O phases to absorb little or no light at 2.4 eV:

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.140 | 0.00017 |
| 15 | 0.381 | −0.00002 |
| 21 | 0.587 | 0.00007 |
| 25 | 0.698 | 0.0002 |
| 29 | 0.807 | **0.00096** |

Every value is close to zero, which fits the expectation. MgO, the MgSb₂O₆ trirutile and Mg₄Sb₂O₉ all have band gaps too wide to absorb 2.4 eV photons. Index 29 is about 5× higher than the next-best reading. That is consistent with Sb-rich oxide phases (such as Sb₂O₄ or Sb₆O₁₃) absorbing weakly, but I didn't confirm this with XRD.

I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements. I also didn't test indices 26–28, so a slightly higher value could sit elsewhere near the Sb-rich end. Even so, EQE anywhere on this line is likely to be negligible.
